defects: Restricted to the real field ℝ only, whereas gold is stated for general RCLike 𝕜 (covers ℝ and ℂ)

Assumes domain and codomain are the same finite-dimensional space ℝ^n (square matrix A), whereas gold allows V to be a different (possibly infinite-dimensional) inner product space, covering isometric embeddings into strictly larger spaces where the notion of determinant doesn't directly apply

Represents the map concretely as a matrix acting on Fin n → ℝ rather than as an abstract linear isometry between general inner product spaces U, V, losing the generality of the 'normDet' construction defined via orthonormal bases for maps of possibly differing dimensions

Conclusion uses ordinary Matrix.det/abs value instead of the generalized normDet, which is only equivalent to |det A| in the square same-dimension case captured by gold as a special instance, not the full statement
